title: Pick your airline seat by texting an agent
summary: A user gave the Instinct agent on WhatsApp her Delta reservation number; she says it found the booking and chose her window seat without checking back.
agent_role: The agent looked up the booking from a reservation number and selected a window seat online. The human only sent the request over WhatsApp.
outcome: Author reports the agent booked her window seat without needing the airline app or customer service.
what_they_did: The poster tried Instinct, an agent you message on WhatsApp that acts for you. She sent it her Delta reservation number and asked for a window seat. It found the booking and picked the seat on the airline's site.
how_it_went: She says it got the seat without her opening the airline app or calling customer service. It did not come back to her for confirmation before acting.
worth_knowing: The agent acted without asking her to confirm first. That was fine for a seat choice, but you may want to require approval for anything that costs money.
prompt: Here is my airline booking: [airline], reservation number [reservation number], last name [last name]. Find my booking on the airline's website and check which seats are available on [flight]. I want a [window/aisle] seat, ideally [front/back of the plane]. Show me the best two or three options and any extra fees. Wait for my approval before selecting a seat or paying anything.

curation.rationale: A real but thin example: a chat-based agent found an airline booking and picked a window seat on its own. Most of the post is opinion, with few details, but daily-life use earns it a place.
